answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a verifiable chain of sequential modular squarings before it can participate. Each squaring depends on the previous result, so GPUs cannot shorten the elapsed time for a single identity by parallelizing that chain. An attacker may run many clones concurrently, but each needs its own full computation, making identities costly in physical time; nectar, walnut, and ridge mark distinct checkpoints, not shortcuts.
